ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and senior managers against the United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List, the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2020 list, the New Zealand Police terrorists designations under the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002, OFAC SDN List, and EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; screening is performed at client acceptance and on a rolling 24-hour alert basis via a commercial sanctions database; any Politically Exposed Person (PEP) trigger must escalate to senior management with enhanced due diligence and ongoing transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register (https://app.companiesoffice.govt.nz/companies)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin script or Te Reo Maori; if a proposed name is in a non-Latin or non-English language, an English transliteration and a translation of the meaning must be submitted; all names must not be offensive, misleading, suggest government connection, or contravene section 22 of the Companies Act 1993; the suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd' is required unless an exemption applies.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: International (in a financial or development context)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may submit an amended name via the online portal; request written reasons from the Registrar under section 22(4) of the Companies Act 1993; file a written reconsideration application to the Companies Office within 20 working days of the refusal; if rejected a second time, apply for administrative review by the Registrar or judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016; reservations can be renewed for a further 20 working days if the renewal application is filed before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for administrative and correspondence purposes only; the registered office must be a physical street address in New Zealand at which legal documents can be served and which is open during normal business hours; serviced offices or virtual offices with physical reception facilities are acceptable; a mere PO Box or non-physical address is prohibited. The crew recruitment agency should maintain a physical operational or representative office, at minimum, to support payroll and crew contract substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated below 5% annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection for a standard low-risk crewing agency, rising to 15-20% if the entity becomes an AML/CFT reporting entity and is subject to Department of Internal Affairs or Financial Markets Authority supervisory site visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 10 to 15 (formation and incorporation of companies), section 12 (application for incorporation), section 13 (certificate of incorporation), section 14 (common seal), section 15 (registered office and address for service), section 16 (constitution), sections 128 to 153 (shareholder and director administration and directors' duties), sections 156 to 161 (appointment and cessation of directors), sections 200 to 203 (issue and allotment of shares), and sections 221 to 230 (annual return and register maintenance), together with the Financial Reporting Act 2013 for reporting relief applicable to exempt and small companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); filings are submitted electronically through the New Zealand Companies Register at companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZCN1 – Application for Incorporation of a Company under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993, filed via the online Companies Register together with the NZCN3 consent-to-appointment forms for directors and shareholders, the registered office declaration, and any adopted constitution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by the Companies Act 1993; New Zealand companies are capitalized by no-par-value shares, and the board may issue shares for any consideration determined at allotment. No escrow account, capital deposit, or bank certificate is required for incorporation; however, a fully paid-up allotment of ordinary shares is recommended to satisfy bank due diligence and the Maritime New Zealand financial-eligibility review for the seafarer recruitment and placement service licence.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (FORMED UNDER THE COMPANIES ACT 1993). RESOLVED, as follows: (1) That the incorporation of the Company under the Companies Act 1993 be and is hereby ratified and confirmed, and the certificate of incorporation and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) be received and recorded in the registers of the Company. (2) That the constitution, if adopted, be approved, adopted, and ratified, and that a copy be filed at the registered office. (3) That the subscribers' share allotments set out in the application for incorporation be and are hereby ratified, and the directors be authorised to issue share certificates and to maintain the share register in accordance with sections 200 to 217 of the Companies Act 1993. (4) That the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [full street address, including level, building, city, and postcode] and that the address for service be recorded with the Companies Office. (5) That [Name A] be and is hereby appointed as Managing Director, [Name B] be and is hereby appointed as Finance Director, [Name C] be and is hereby appointed as Corporate Secretary (if applicable), and [Name D] be and is hereby appointed as Compliance Officer for the seafarer recruitment and placement service, each to hold office until removal pursuant to the Companies Act 1993 and any applicable constitution. (6) That the directors so appointed be authorised, jointly or severally, to open corporate bank accounts with [bank name], to execute account signatory mandates, and to activate SWIFT wire and multi-currency payroll payment rails. (7) That the Managing Director and Compliance Officer be and are hereby authorised to prepare and submit all applications, forms, and supporting dossiers to Maritime New Zealand for the Approved Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Service Certificate under MLC 2006 Regulation 1.4, and to liaise with the Environmental Protection Authority, Fire and Emergency New Zealand, and WorkSafe New Zealand in respect of all physical premises and occupational health and safety clearances. (8) That all actions taken prior to this resolution in connection with the incorporation and the opening of the Company's tax registrations with Inland Revenue be and are hereby ratified and confirmed. DATED [DATE]. SIGNED by the Sole Director / Chairperson of the Board: [SIGNATURE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Search and NZBN Pre-Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office via the online Companies Register name availability search and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registry portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a reserved-name and available-name search against the Companies Register and the NZBN database to confirm that the proposed name is distinctive, not identical or confusingly similar to an existing company or reserved name, and does not contain prohibited words under the Companies Act 1993 and the Companies (Names) regulations. Submit a name reservation request if the client requires priority, and record the NZBN pre-allocated to the intended entity. Ensure that the proposed name does not imply any Crown, harbourmaster, or maritimesafety affiliation that could mislead crew applicants.
required_dossiers: Name availability search result printout
Client instruction letter identifying the legal entity and business scope
List of proposed shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners
Declaration of no objection from any existing holder of a similar maritime or crewing mark, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar or prohibited, submit a new name application or request registrar reconsideration under the Companies Act 1993; alternatively reserve and register a revised distinctive name and update the incorporation application accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Statutory Consents and Optional Constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (final custodian); executed before a lawyer, notary public, or an authorised attestor for foreign signatories.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the consent-to-appointment forms for each director and shareholder, together with the company constitution (if adopted), in accordance with sections 12 and 16 of the Companies Act 1993. The registered office address and address for service must be a physical New Zealand address. Each director must consent in writing to act as a director, and each subscriber must consent to the allotment of shares. For the International Company variant with non-resident ownership, the governing documentation should include a non-resident ownership declaration and confirmation that the entity does not carry on business through a New Zealand physical ship-operating facility, while remaining subject to the Companies Act 1993 governance duties.
required_dossiers: Form NZCN3 consent to appointment of each director
Shareholder consent to incorporation and share allotment
Optional constitution of the company executed by all subscribers
Certified copy of passport or national identity document of each director and shareholder
Proof of residential and business address of each director and shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective or incomplete consents will be queried by the Companies Office; cure by re-execution or amendment of the consent forms and resubmission within the statutory response period without loss of priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Application for Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge Form NZCN1 electronically through the Companies Register, together with the consent forms and the constitution, and pay the prescribed filing fee by credit/debit card or online bank transfer. Declare the New Zealand registered office, the address for service, the intended principal business (ISIC 5222 – activities of seafarer recruitment and vessel crew management agencies), and the full details of the first directors and shareholders. The application must be authorised by each shareholder and director; electronic signatures are accepted by the Companies Office portal.
required_dossiers: Form NZCN1 – Application for Incorporation of a Company
Form NZCN3 director consent forms
Shareholder consent forms
Constitution (if adopted)
Registered office address declaration and landlord consent if the premises are to be used as a registered office
Anti-money-laundering customer due diligence pack (identity, source of funds, and structure chart)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a query or requisition under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant must cure the indicated defects and refile within the response window; if the certificate is issued erroneously, apply to the Registrar for rectification of the register under the correction provisions of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN, and Corporate Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and NZBN Registrar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation from the Companies Register and retrieve the allocated New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). The company comes into existence on the date of incorporation. Immediately establish the statutory registers, including the share register, directors' register, and addresses register, and issue the initial share certificates to the subscribers. Record the registered office and address for service in the internal minute book, and endorse the corporate name seal (if a common seal is adopted).
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
NZBN notification letter
Share register in the form required by section 221 of the Companies Act 1993
Directors' register
Registered office declaration
Minute book and statutory records binder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical error or the registers cannot be generated, apply to the Companies Office for a replacement certificate through the self-service portal or request a registrar correction; no re-incorporation is required for clerical correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Tax Registrations and Employer Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue (Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for an IRD number using the online business registration service, and concurrently register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if the expected taxable supply turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 per 12-month period or if voluntary GST registration is elected. Register as an employer for PAYE if the crew hiring and payroll services will engage New Zealand-based employees or seconded crew, and register for fringe benefit tax (FBT) if non-cash benefits are provided to employees. Provide the IRD number, NZBN, and financial year-end election (normally 31 March unless a balanced date is approved). The company should also register for the multi-currency payroll and SWIFT wire payment ecosystem to ensure international crew salary remittance capabilities.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
NZBN confirmation
Directors' identity documents and consent forms
Corporate bank account details
Expected turnover and GST projection worksheet
Employer payroll and PAYE commencement declaration, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue queries the registration, respond with a consolidated clarification pack within the notice period; pending IRD number allocation, the company may proceed with bank opening under a certificate of good-standing from the Companies Office; retroactive tax registration date can be aligned with the incorporation date upon correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Account and Payment Rails Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered New Zealand bank (e.g., ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac, or a licensed non-bank financial institution approved by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the corporate account application with a licensed bank, presenting the certificate of incorporation, NZBN, constitution, and board resolution on signatories. Complete SWIFT wire activation and multi-currency payroll facility enrolment, ensuring the account supports NZD, USD, EUR, GBP, and AUD settlements for international crew wages. Provide the bank with the AML/CFT due diligence pack, the beneficial ownership structure, and the nature and volume of expected crew payroll transactions under ISIC 5222. The bank will perform a CDD assessment and may request a revenue forecast and sample payroll schedule.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN
Constitution and first board resolution authorising bank signatories
Directors' and shareholders' passport copies and proof of address
AML/CFT beneficial ownership and source-of-funds declaration
Revenue forecast and crew payroll projection
SWIFT and multi-currency service application forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or deferred, furnish supplementary beneficial ownership declarations, an updated source-of-funds trail, or a chartered accountant reference; if the bank still declines, approach an alternate licensed bank or engage an approved payment aggregator that reports to the Resident authority for SWIFT and payroll rails.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maritime New Zealand MLC 2006 Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Service Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Maritime New Zealand (Maritime NZ), the competent maritime authority under the Maritime Transport Act 1994 and the Maritime Labour Convention 2006 (MLC 2006).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal application for approval to operate a seafarer recruitment and placement service, together with a compliance manual demonstrating alignment with MLC 2006 Regulation 1.4 and the New Zealand maritime rules on crew welfare. The compliance manual must address the following: transparent fee charging (seafarers shall not bear the recruitment costs or placement fees), robust complaint handling procedures, medical and certification verification of crew, maintenance of up-to-date crew registers, payment protection and repatriation arrangements, and the appointment of a licensed compliance officer. Provide evidence of adequate insurance or financial security to compensate seafarers for any losses arising from the agency's failure of duty. The application is assessed by Maritime NZ and, upon approval, an Approved Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Service Certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Maritime NZ application for approval of a seafarer recruitment and placement service
Certificate of incorporation and NZBN
Business plan evidencing crewing agency operations under ISIC 5222
MLC 2006 compliance manual and complaint handling procedure
Crew fee schedule and zero-charge-to-seafarer policy
Crew medical and certification verification procedure
Insurance or financial security certificate
Copy of the first board resolution appointing the compliance officer
Criminal record checks for directors and key compliance personnel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Maritime NZ may issue a request for further information or a preliminary refusal; the applicant is entitled to submit supplementary compliance evidence within the specified response period, and a final refusal may be appealed to the District Court under the Maritime Transport Act 1994 or by way of judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil Defense, Fire Safety, Structural, and Occupational Health and Safety Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), the relevant territorial authority building consent department, and WorkSafe New Zealand.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the physical premises from which the crew recruitment and processing business is conducted, obtain or upgrade the Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) under the Building Act 2004, including the compliance schedule for any fire suppression systems, emergency lighting, and means of escape. Submit an application for approval of a fire evacuation scheme to FENZ where the premises are covered by an evacuation scheme requirement. Arrange a structural load inspection certificate for any fit-out, partition, or mezzanine structure used for crew interviews or training rooms. Undertake a Workplace Health and Safety (HSW) risk assessment under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 and register for supervised/self-managed work if required by WorkSafe NZ. This clearance is mandatory before employee-facing crew processing or new hire onboarding sessions commence.
required_dossiers: Application for fire evacuation scheme approval (FENZ form)
Building Warrant of Fitness and compliance schedule
Structural load inspection certificate and engineer's report
Workplace health and safety risk assessment and induction procedure
Fire safety and emergency evacuation certificate
Certificate of acceptance for the premises occupancy under the Building Act 2004
Landlord consent for the registered office and operational premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FENZ or territorial authority issues a notice of deficiency or prevents occupation, remedy the building or fire-safety defects through the engineer's and licensed building practitioner's work and apply for re-inspection; appeal an unsatisfactory building inspection decision to the Registrar of Building System Performance within the statutory appeal window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Maritime New Zealand (Maritime NZ) is the competent authority under the Maritime Transport Act 1994 and the Maritime Labour Convention 2006 (MLC 2006), responsible for approving seafarer recruitment and placement services; parallel workplace and premises compliance oversight is exercised by WorkSafe New Zealand, Fire and Emergency New Zealand, and the relevant territorial local authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Approved Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Service Certificate (issued under MLC 2006 Regulation 1.4 and administered by Maritime New Zealand).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of New Zealand, with delegated resource consent and trade waste functions exercisable by the regional council and territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 – Permitted Activity. The crew recruitment and vessel crew management agency occupies a standard office and interview facility; no full EIA report or integrated resource consent is required for the brokerage and payroll operations. A resource consent or EIA screening would only be triggered by portside physical crew-change accommodation, crew medical quarantine facilities, vessel berthing infrastructure, or marine discharge activities, none of which fall within the scoped corporate vehicle.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: office ablution and sanitary discharges may be discharged only to the municipal sewer system and must comply with the local council's Trade Waste Bylaw and the National Environmental Standards for Sources of Drinking Water where applicable; no industrial process wastewater or marine discharge is permitted. VOCs and Air Emissions: indoor office operations may not exceed the Ministry for the Environment ambient air quality guidelines for volatile organic compounds; use of solvent-based printing, bonding, or cleaning agents in crew document processing areas must be within the occupational exposure limits of the Australian/New Zealand workplace exposure standards. Waste Handling: general commercial waste must be removed by an approved waste carrier under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008; hazardous wastes, including printer cartridges, cleaning solvents, and any disposable medical or crew safety inspection equipment, must be managed by a certified hazardous waste contractor with the requisite environmental manifest documentation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) approval of the premises' fire evacuation scheme and the Building Warrant of Fitness under the Building Act 2004, including structural load inspection certificates for any mezzanine or fit-out areas used for crew interviews and medical checks; workplace clearance issued by WorkSafe New Zealand under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, encompassing a verified risk assessment, first-aid provisioning, and emergency response plans for office and crew processing activities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue / Te Tari Taake) of New Zealand; online portal 'myIR' at myIR.ird.govt.nz; corporate registry functions are performed by the New Zealand Companies Office, with the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) as the public business identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned or non-resident International Company (custom entity type CK_IC) establishing a crew recruitment and vessel crew management agency in New Zealand: (1) incorporate the company under the Companies Act 1993 or, if the foreign IC is already incorporated offshore, register as an overseas company under Part 18 of the Companies Act 1993 and obtain an NZBN; (2) apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number using form IR742 'Registration for a non-resident company' or the myIR on-boarding application; (3) register for Goods and Services Tax using form GST101 or myIR when taxable supplies to be made in New Zealand will exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, or elect voluntary registration earlier; (4) register as a PAYE employer via myIR if the agency will employ seafarers, office staff, or NZ-based crew; (5) if the agency supplies remote or cross-border payroll and crew management services to NZ-resident ship operators, complete the non-resident supplier GST registration for remote services under the same NZD 60,000 threshold; (6) obtain a New Zealand Customs Service client code (NZECS) only if the agency also exports physical goods or arranges international cargo; pure crew recruitment and payroll services do not require a customs client code.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: under the ELF_CUSTOM_CK_IC classification, the International Company is a non-resident company whose central management and control sit outside New Zealand and which derives no New Zealand-sourced income; it therefore falls outside the New Zealand income tax net under the Income Tax Act 2007 residence and source rules. If the IC becomes centrally managed and controlled in New Zealand (s YC(2) Income Tax Act 2007) or carries on a taxable activity through a permanent establishment in New Zealand, it will instead be taxed on a worldwide or New Zealand-source basis respectively at the 28% corporate rate, with the imputation credit regime applying to resident shareholders.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' election; entity classification is primarily determined by statute. The principal elections relevant to the CK_IC are: (a) Look-Through Company election under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, giving pass-through treatment for qualifying closely held companies; (b) GST group registration election under s 55 of the GST Act 1985, allowing the IC and its NZ subsidiaries to be treated as one GST-registered person; (c) financial arrangement rule election under the Income Tax Act 2007 (IFRS, fair value, or base price adjustment methods) for payroll and crew receivables; (d) hybrid mismatch response elections under Part 6B of the Income Tax Act 2007 where a foreign trust or offshore shareholder ring is present; (e) GST taxable period and accounting basis elections (payments, invoice, or hybrid basis) filed with Inland Revenue; and (f) provisional tax calculation basis elections (standard, estimation, ratio, or GST ratio methods).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (No 141), administered by Inland Revenue as a national, unitary consumption tax; there is no provincial or state sales and use tax in New Zealand.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies made or deemed to be made in New Zealand within any 12-month period (s 51(1) GST Act 1985), including by non-resident suppliers of 'remote services' to New Zealand residents under ss 54B to 54H GST Act 1985. A crew recruitment agency with a physical NZ office is subject to the same threshold for its recruitment, training, medical, and payroll services supplied in NZ; for services supplied to non-resident shipowners for crews on foreign-flag vessels operating outside NZ territorial waters, the agency can rely on zero-rating rather than the registration threshold if the supply is outside NZ.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, invoice digital stamping, or supplier API pre-clearance. Tax invoices must contain the particulars required under the GST Act 1985 (seller name and GST number, invoice date, description, GST-inclusive/exclusive amounts). Optional Peppol BIS 3.0 B2B/B2G e-invoicing is available through accredited access points; no government approval is required. Mandatory electronic reporting exists for: (i) GST returns (GST101), which must be filed electronically via myIR or a gateway system for registered persons with large turnover and for all GST-registered businesses with monthly or two-monthly taxable periods required by the Commissioner; and (ii) 'payday filing' of Employment Information by every employer, which is mandatory through myIR or payroll software for each payday. There is no fiscal printer, continuous audit file, or digital stamp regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods zero-rating under s 11 GST Act 1985 applies where the goods are exported from New Zealand within 28 days after the time of supply, with the exporter retaining shipping and customs documentation. Services zero-rating under s 11A GST Act 1985 applies to services supplied to a person not resident in New Zealand who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, provided the services are not: (a) supplied to a person present in New Zealand, (b) directly in connection with land in New Zealand, (c) physically performed in New Zealand, or (d) otherwise acquired for consumption in NZ. The crew recruitment agency can zero-rate its international crew management fees (vessel coverage scheduling, payroll administration, visa and travel logistics, compliance and vetting) when invoiced to a non-resident shipowner or ship manager for crews employed aboard foreign-flag vessels operating wholly outside New Zealand territorial waters and not engaged in coastal trade of New Zealand. Services physically performed in New Zealand, such as interviews, medicals, pre-embarkation training, and crew dispatch from a New Zealand port, are standard-rated at 15% unless they qualify as reimbursements/disbursements or another zero-rating exception. The 'remote services' zero-rating under s 11AB GST Act 1985 may apply to digital or distance B2B services supplied to non-resident recipients, but not where the services require physical performance in New Zealand; the agency must maintain separate invoicing and time-sheet evidence for any NZ-physical service components.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service export declaration (NZECS/e-Cert) evidencing export of goods where physical export occurs; not applicable to pure crew services
Ocean Bill of Lading, seaway bill, or intermodal transport document covering crew travels or vessel supplies where applicable

Fully executed Crew Management and Recruitment Agreement with the non-resident shipowner or ship manager, stating the non-resident recipient, foreign-flag vessel, place of performance, and GST treatment

Commercial invoice pack, crew payroll records, and monthly disbursement statements demonstrating that the supply is made to a person not resident in New Zealand and absent from New Zealand at the time of supply

Bank inward remittance advice / foreign currency deposit certificate from a New Zealand registered bank showing settlement in foreign currency within the pipeline-standard 180-day inward remittance period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit zero-rated GST claims and retrospectively assess GST at 15% if the documentary substantiation is incomplete or the recipient is later found to be a New Zealand resident, present in New Zealand, or the crew services were physically performed in New Zealand. The statutory amendment time bar is generally 4 years from the date of assessment under ss 108 and 108A of the Tax Administration Act 1994, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud, evasion, or long-term failure to file. Shortfall penalties under Part 9 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply: 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, and 150% for evasion or an abusive tax position, together with use-of-money interest at the statutory rate. Clawback also arises where the agency issues credit notes or changes the supply itinerary after the vessel has undertaken New Zealand coastal legs or crew have performed services in New Zealand territorial waters; directors and officers can face personal liability under the corporate officer penalty provisions for assisting in a seriously incorrect GST return.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully open capital account with no exchange-control legislation in force since the deregulation of 1984. The New Zealand dollar is freely convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions. The Cook Islands, although a self-governing territory in free association with New Zealand, uses the New Zealand dollar as its official currency and applies no separate exchange-control regime. A Cook Islands International Company faces no statutory restrictions on the repatriation of profits, dividends, return of share capital, repayment of shareholder loans, or remittance of liquidation proceeds. The only compliance gates for currency conversion and outward remittance are bank-level anti-money-laundering and countering-financing-of-terrorism verification obligations, including source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership documentation. No central-bank approval is required for any inward or outward payment. Profit remittance is fully current-account free, subject solely to corporate solvency documentation and standard documentary compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender rules apply in New Zealand or the Cook Islands. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation of export receipts, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to credit export proceeds to a designated local currency account. A Cook Islands International Company operating a ship crew recruitment agency may receive crewing fees, commission income, and management fees in any currency, hold those proceeds in any jurisdiction, and convert them at commercial dealing rates without any obligation to surrender foreign currency to the central bank or to any licensed dealer. The only applicable requirement is that all transactions be recorded in the company's books and that the economic substance threshold, if any, be satisfied under the Cook Islands International Companies Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_operational_note: The term 'central bank authority' is understood to mean the Reserve Bank of New Zealand as the monetary authority issuing the currency used by the entity, together with the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission which supervises banks, trust companies, and international companies within the Cook Islands pursuant to the Banking Act 1987 and the Financial Supervisory Commission Act 2004. All references to central-bank approval in this dossier are read accordingly.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility with material legal constraints. New Zealand-incorporated or licensed electronic money institutions (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, and other domestic non-bank payment service providers) generally decline to onboard a Cook Islands International Company due to its classification as an offshore, tax-exempt legal entity without New Zealand tax residence. Such entities are automatically flagged for enhanced due diligence under local AML/CFT rules and frequently excluded by emi platform onboarding policies. A small number of specialist cross-border payment platforms that accept Pacific-rim offshore companies may offer virtual multi-currency IBAN settlement, but they impose strict transaction velocity limits, payroll-batch restrictions, and require nominated compliance-officer sign-off and audited source-of-funds documentation. Legal constraint: no EMI may provide true deposit-taking services in New Zealand or the Cook Islands; an EMI account is only a payment-rail tool and cannot serve as the sole treasury repository. The primary banking anchor must remain a licensed bank in the Cook Islands or New Zealand.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of at least one director or the authorized signatory is generally required for the initial onboarding interview at Bank of the Cook Islands, ANZ Cook Islands, Westpac Cook Islands, and Pacific Private Bank. Remote onboarding is possible only where the AML/CFT compliance officer conducts an equivalent face-to-face video verification session supported by notarized or apostilled identity documents, a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation, a certificate of good standing, a register of directors and shareholders, a beneficial-ownership declaration, and a certified trust deed or nominee declaration if applicable. New Zealand domestic banks normally require an in-person interview at a New Zealand branch for foreign registered entities; remote opening is available only to New Zealand tax-resident companies. Where no physical office exists in the Cook Islands or New Zealand, a registered local agent or legal counsel must attend the interview in person and present original board resolutions and a business plan substantiating the crew-recruitment commercial model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore International Company with tax-exempt status assessed as a shell or brass-plate entity lacking economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic-substance file: lease or ownership deed for a physical crewing-office premises in Rarotonga or Auckland, employment contracts of locally resident crewing managers, monthly payroll records for local staff, corporate bank statements demonstrating active crew-payroll and invoicing flows, audited financial statements prepared by a licensed Cook Islands or New Zealand chartered accountant, an annual return confirming board-meeting minutes, and a board resolution articulating the commercial rationale for the Cook Islands structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume multi-currency payroll disbursed to seafarers of multiple nationalities on vessels flagged in various jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-beneficiary crew employment agreements, seafarer discharge-book or maritime identification documents, vessel-manning agreements with shipowners, underlying crew-supply or invoice-and-debit-note documentation, a verified beneficiary master list, payroll run summaries in NZD and USD or EUR, and an attestation confirming screening of all crew against RBNZ, OFAC, UN, EU, and UK sanctions lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity caused by nominee shareholders or a trust overlay above the International Company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A current register of beneficial owners filed with the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission, the complete trust deed and any settlement deeds, AEOI/CRS self-certification forms and tax-residence statements for each ultimate beneficial owner, the nominee-services agreement, and a corporate-ownership chart signed by a licensed trustee or registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a high-risk or non-transparent source jurisdiction with ambiguous remittance purpose codes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder source-of-wealth letter, audited bank statements of the remitting shareholder, an executed share-subscription agreement, the underlying commercial contract or business-purchase agreement explaining the funding purpose, a flow-of-funds diagram showing the corporate-group structure, and a legal opinion from Cook Islands or New Zealand counsel confirming legal origin of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound payments to maritime subcontractors, vessel suppliers, or manning agents potentially connected to sanctioned shipping
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vessel name and IMO number, current ISM and ISPS certificates, ownership and beneficial-ownership disclosure from the shipowner, flag-state registry extract, classification-society certificates, the master crew-supply agreement, and third-party due-diligence reports covering sanctions, anti-bribery, corruption, and maritime security screening.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections to a Cook Islands International Company are unrestricted and require no central-bank approval. Compliant routing protocol: the remitting shareholder or group entity issues a SWIFT MT103 from its own bank with the remittance information field containing the International Company's registration number and the purpose description 'Capital Injection into International Company' or 'Share Subscription'. The receiving bank will require the company's board resolution authorizing the account opening and the injection, a register of beneficial owners, and source-of-funds evidence. Where the injection is structured as a shareholder advance or intercompany loan, an executed loan agreement with interest rate, maturity, and repayment schedule must be lodged with the receiving bank. NZD-leg payments in New Zealand are cleared through the Exchange Settlement Account System operated by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand with real-time gross settlement finality; USD, EUR, and AUD wires are processed via the correspondent banking network and confirmed by SWIFT MT103 acknowledgments. For Cook Islands-based receiving banks, settlement occurs through their SWIFT agency relationships, and funds are credited to the IC account upon receipt of the cover payment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for crew payroll, advances, and trade settlements flow through the following clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 single-wire transfers for individual seafarer salary payments, repatriation advances, emergency medical disbursements, and deferred-wage settlements; (ii) ISO 20022 pacs.008 payment messages for batch multi-currency payroll runs delivered through the bank's host-to-host API or SWIFT global-payment service, with each payment carrying a structured remittance reference; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit issued subject to UCP 600 for large-scale crew-provisioning contracts, vessel-operator service settlements, or procurement of marine supplies; (iv) standby letters of credit (SWIFT MT760) where the agency must provide a performance guarantee or collateral to shipowners or government authorities; (v) local NZD clearing via Payments New Zealand infrastructure where NZD-denominated payments to crew welfare funds or domestic subcontractors must be settled next-day net. All outbound MT103 messages must include the agency invoice number, crew or contract reference, and comply with the paying bank's sanctions-screening requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts (T+2 value date) for conversion between NZD, USD, EUR, AUD, and GBP at commercial dealing rates without requiring RBNZ approval.

Outright FX forward contracts with tenors up to 24 months for fixing future payroll and receivables conversions; permitted without transactional documentary proof under New Zealand market practice, although banks may request an underlying crewing services contract for compliance review.
Foreign-exchange swaps with matched near leg and far leg, such as NZD/USD, permitted for working-capital smoothing and temporary liquidity bridging.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in less-liquid crosses involving NZD against emerging-market currencies such as PHP, IDR, VND, and BDT, used to hedge crew home-country remittance exposure without requiring physical settlement in the illiquid currency.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) for multi-year financing of vessel-crew recruitment contracts or acquisition funding, permitted under an ISDA 2002 master agreement with a licensed New Zealand bank or an international bank branch.

FX options and collar strategies, including cancelable forwards, permitted for premium-limited hedging of payroll tender risk, subject to a board-approved derivatives-capacity resolution and compliance with applicable conduct standards.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing anniversary of the company's incorporation date; must be filed every year within 15 working days after the date of the Annual Meeting, but no later than the anniversary of incorporation if no meeting is held
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 200 (approx. USD 120); continued non-compliance for 6 months or more triggers formal warning, and persistent default may lead to removal from the New Zealand Register under the Companies Act 1993, resulting in company strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation Report (previously Annual Return filed with Companies Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 working days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation; exemption applies if the company ceases to carry on business in New Zealand and satisfies the overseas company deregistration conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file an Annual Confirmation results in NZD 200 late filing penalty; continued failure for six consecutive months may result in deregistration and the Director disqualified under the Companies Act 1993.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Tax Return (Nil or schedular) for Fully Imputed or Exempt International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, generally by 7 July for a standard 31 March balance date; for non-standard balance dates, within 4 months after balance date when no income tax return is required or when return is furnished voluntarily
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 per month up to NZD 1,000 and interest on unpaid tax; continued non-compliance may lead to legal enforcement actions, credit rating impact, and director penalty notices.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Overseas Ship Manning and Crew Recruitment Annual Statutory Report (if licensed as a maritime recruitment agency)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maritime New Zealand (MNZ) and Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: License renewal and operational report by 31 March of each year, or the license anniversary date for crew recruitment and crewing agency permits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or renew the maritime recruitment license results in cessation of lawful operation, penalties up to NZD 50,000 for company, and individual liability for directors under the Maritime Transport Act 1994.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ships and Maritime Crew Agency Annual Disclosure to the Registrar of Maritime Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maritime New Zealand (MNZ) Registrar of Maritime Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 1 month after the end of the reporting year (31 December), covering seafarer employment agreements and collective bargaining agreements in effect
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with maritime labour certificate requirements results in prohibition from providing crew to foreign-flagged vessels, monetary penalties of up to NZD 20,000, and potential cancellation of the crewing agency permit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Resident Withholding Tax (RWT) and Employer Annual Return (IR348 / PAYE Annual Schedule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payroll annual reconciliation due 30 June following the end of the tax year (31 March); employer monthly schedules by the 20th day of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to NZD 500 plus use-of-money interest; non-declaration of withholding taxes may trigger criminal liability and director penalty assessments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is required if the company is a 'large company' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, defined as total assets exceeding NZD 60 million, or total revenue exceeding NZD 30 million, or has 50 or more full-time equivalent employees; for an international company exempt-zone entity, audit is also mandatory if shareholders holding 5% or more request a financial statement audit; small-to-medium companies may provide unaudited annual financial statements unless audit is convened by shareholder requisition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS) for for-profit entities; Tier 2 New Zealand Accounting Standards (NZAS) for entities without public accountability; full IFRS permitted where adopted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand maintains a centralized Beneficial Ownership Register administered under the Companies Act 1993 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; every company must maintain an accurate and up-to-date register of significant controllers (25% or more ownership or control) and disclose changes to the Registrar within 10 working days; annual confirmation protocol requires confirmation of the shareholder structure and beneficial ownership at the time of the Annual Confirmation; no separate annual UBO filing fee is imposed, but any change in shareholding or significant control must be lodged immediately with the Companies Office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Significant Controllers (Beneficial Ownership Register)
Minute Book (resolutions and proceedings of shareholders and directors)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: NZD 850 – NZD 2,500 (approx. USD 510 – USD 1,500) per annum for professional registered office and corporate secretarial services including the offshore shipping/crew agency licensing support, subject to agent fee schedules.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: NZD 12,000 – NZD 35,000 (approx. USD 7,200 – USD 21,000) for a Tier 1 or Tier 2 statutory audit of a holdco with minimal trading activity; smaller unaudited financial statement compilation fee is typically NZD 2,500 – NZD 6,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (New Zealand standard corporate rate); 0% for a qualifying Cook Islands International Company (Tax_Exempt_Zone) under the International Companies Act 1981-82 in respect of non-New Zealand-sourced income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective rate on foreign-source profits for a Cook Islands IC; NZ imputation regime does not apply; no NZ capital gains tax on most assets; NZ loss carry-forward is indefinite subject to 49% shareholder continuity (schema placeholder 5 retained; not a statutory limit for NZ-resident companies)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cook Islands IC: annual Economic Substance Declaration and annual return of information to the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC); NZ-resident exposure: IR4 Company Tax Return filed via Inland Revenue myIR (IRD) e-filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (both jurisdictions; provisional tax in NZ may be paid in three installments if NZ-resident)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: NZ IR4 standard balance date 31 March: return due 7 July; if non-standard balance date, due 3 months after balance date (4 months if electronically filed); Cook Islands ESR declaration due within 12 months of financial year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales, dividends, interest and other income (turnover)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with New Zealand-source income only must include NZ-source gross income; a tax-exempt Cook Islands IC with no NZ-source income is not required to file IR4
Expenses must be allocated on a justified apportionment basis for NZ-source activities; no deduction for amounts diverted to tax-exempt related entities unless arm's length

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before tax (accounting statement adjusted for tax adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for non-deductible items (e.g., entertaining expenses, penalties) and TP adjustments under s GC 6-GC 15 ITA 2007

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss offsets and subpart BH loss provisions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss offsets require 49% continuity; a non-resident company must also satisfy the 'ring-fencing' rules for rental and other classes of income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax credits (RWT, PAYE, provisional tax paid, imputation credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies claim credits for NZ RWT and foreign dividend withholding payments; the tax-exempt IC will have no NZ tax credits arising

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable on taxable income (28% for companies)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the IC is managed and controlled from New Zealand it is NZ tax resident and taxed on worldwide income at 28%; otherwise only NZ-source income is taxed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual income tax (tax liability less credits; triggers provisional tax for following year)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with NZ-source income over the $2,500 threshold are liable for provisional tax in three installments

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credit account (ICA) balance (debit or credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned companies may elect the FDP (foreign dividend withholding payment) system; a Cook Islands IC does not maintain an NZ ICA if exempt

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carried forward / loss offset schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attachment of loss continuity schedules; losses cannot be utilised by non-residents except through NZ-source activities

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty NZ$250 per month or part-month for companies (maximum NZ$500); late payment penalty: 4% initial of unpaid tax plus 1% per month thereafter; use-of-money interest charged daily at the underpayment rate (currently approximately 8.4% per annum); failure to file an Economic Substance Declaration in the Cook Islands attracts penalty of NZ$5,000 (individual) / NZ$20,000 (company) plus criminal sanctions for false declarations (my best knowledge)

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: NZ NRWT on dividends: 30% (standard) / 0% for a Cook Islands IC distributing tax-exempt foreign-source profits where no NZ residence is established; if NZ-resident, a 30% NRWT applies subject to a DTA reduction (e.g., 15% for Australia, 5% for a 10%+ corporate shareholder under several treaties). No DTA exists between NZ and Cook Islands, so treaty relief is not available between those two territories.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief on NZ-sourced dividends, interest or royalties: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction of residence; (2) complete NZ Inland Revenue form IR372 (Certificate of residence for DTA/RCA/NRWT rates) and lodge with the payer or IM tax return; (3) retain a fully executed TRC in e-records to support the 0%, 5%, 10% or 15% treaty rate; (4) if the payer withheld at the higher domestic rate, file a non-resident withholding tax refund/rebate application (form IR255) within the statutory period; (5) ensure treaty entitlement under the limitation of benefits provisions (economic substance test).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: NZ domestic NRWT: interest 15%, royalties 15%; approved issuer levy (AIL) on interest at 2% may apply if the borrower is an approved issuer and the lender is a non-associated offshore lender; treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 10% or 0% (bank interest) and royalties to 10% or 5%; since no NZ-Cook Islands DTA exists, a Cook Islands IC will generally face 15% NZ NRWT on NZ-source interest and royalties, subject to the AIL alternative for interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: There is no statutory Local/Master File filing in NZ, but contemporaneous TP documentation must be prepared and retained when aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZ$10 million per annum (goods) or NZ$1 million (services, interest, and intangibles); for a Cook Islands IC, annual ESR records must be filed with the FSC for any relevant activity regardless of value; NZ: transfer pricing documentation / benchmarking must be produced within 30 days of an IRD request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Cook Islands ESR applies under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Act and Regulations: crew recruitment and vessel crew management are 'relevant activities' (provision of services); the IC must demonstrate (i) direction and management in the Cook Islands, (ii) adequate premises and employees, (iii) real operating expenditure in the Cook Islands, and (iv) core income-generating activities physically carried on there; annual economic substance declaration (Form) required; failure or 'shell' status subjects the IC to penalties, deregistration, and the risk of NZ tax residency (management and control test) with worldwide taxation at 28%.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Diverting New Zealand-source crew recruitment fees to the exempt Cook Islands IC without arm's length remuneration, artificial invoicing of services, or back-to-back contracts designed to avoid NZ tax while management remains in Auckland
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil shortfall penalties under s 141 Tax Administration Act 1994: 150% for evasion (and 100% for abusive tax position); criminal prosecution under s 143A TAA: fine up to NZ$50,000 (first offence) or NZ$100,000 (subsequent) and/or imprisonment up to 5 years; NZ IRD may issue a section 141? 'tax evasion' notice and assess 28% on adjusted profits plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate in, direct, or knowingly permit tax evasion may be convicted personally; under s 143 TAA? (director liability) directors of a company that fails to deduct and pay PAYE/withholding payments may become jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax; reckless trading s 135 Companies Act 1993 exposes directors to personal liability for debts (including tax) and indemnification claims; travel bans and bankruptcy disqualification may follow criminal conviction

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Failure of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the IC as a pure shell with no Cook Islands premises, employees, bank accounts or board meetings; failing to file the annual ESR declaration; nominal shareholders/trustees with no genuine commercial activity in the container/cargo sector
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Cook Islands International Companies Act and ESR regulations: monetary penalties from NZ$10,000 - NZ$20,000 per breach, revocation of international company status and deregistration; the company is also re-characterised as NZ-resident for tax purposes (deemed managed and controlled in NZ), attracting 28% corporate tax on worldwide income and a 30% NRWT on dividends; NZ anti-avoidance rules (s BG 1) may void the arrangement with penalties up to 150% of the shortfall
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Shareholders and directors can be made jointly liable for the taxes owed if the corporate veil is pierced for 'sham', 'alter ego', or 'agency' findings; directors face personal liability to refund trust assets and statutory fines; asset preservation orders and travel bans are available where there is material dissipation risk

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling multi-currency seafarer payroll and Swift wire transfers without AML/CFT registration, customer due diligence (CDD), beneficial ownership identification, or transaction monitoring; accepting cash payroll disbursement without source verification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (NZ) and corresponding Cook Islands AML/CFT Act: penalties up to NZ$10 million for companies and NZ$500,000 for individuals per breach, plus enforceable undertakings and suspension of the statutory licence (maritime crew recruitment requires a licence under the Maritime Employment Act/IS Code); criminal sanctions for money laundering up to 7 years' imprisonment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML/CFT compliance officers and senior managers are personally liable for substantive breaches committed with consent or wilful blindness; directors may be disqualified from managing maritime recruitment agencies, barred from company directorship for up to 5 years, and subject to confiscation orders
